title: China-to-Singapore Industrial Motor Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.target_requirement: Singapore treats industrial AC motors through a standards and energy-efficiency framework using SS standards issued by the Singapore Standards Board under Enterprise Singapore, with IEC 60034 commonly adopted for rotating electrical machines. Covered three-phase motors may also fall under EMA MEPS controls when listed by product type and rating.
rows.china_equivalent: China export files commonly cite GB 18613 for motor IE efficiency classes aligned with IEC 60034-30-1 naming, GB 12665 for cooling-related baseline evidence, and CCC documentation for low-voltage motors where the product is within CCC scope.
rows.gap: Singapore documentation should map the exact product class, rating, phase count, duty, and intended installation to Singapore-recognized SS or IEC evidence and EMA scope. A China GB or CCC package alone does not establish Singapore scope classification or approval.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where the motor is within EMA listed-product MEPS scope; SS or IEC evidence is expected for technical substantiation
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory where GB 18613 and CCC scope apply in China

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Treat the Singapore product-scope decision as a separate classification exercise; do not assume GB 18613 or CCC scope equals EMA or Singapore market scope.

rows.target_requirement: Singapore import and placing-on-market practice requires an in-country responsible supplier or importer able to hold registrations, product records, test evidence, labels, and regulator correspondence for listed or controlled equipment. Product identification should align model numbers, ratings, nameplate data, and energy or safety records.
target_standards: Singapore customs and market surveillance practice
rows.china_equivalent: China export files usually identify the manufacturer, factory, CCC certificate holder where applicable, GB test report number, model family, and nameplate ratings for domestic conformity and export documentation.
rows.gap: Singapore needs a local accountability chain. A Chinese certificate holder or exporter name does not replace the Singapore responsible supplier record, model registration, or regulator-facing file custody.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for listed or controlled products requiring Singapore registration or regulator-facing accountability
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory where China conformity, CCC, or GB documentation requires certificate-holder and model identification

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] A Singapore importer or responsible supplier should be assigned before shipment for any motor expected to need EMA registration, energy evidence, or market-surveillance response.

rows.target_requirement: Singapore applies EMA Minimum Energy Performance Standards for listed motor products and is directionally aligned with IE2 or IE3 requirements depending on the covered category and implementation schedule. Covered three-phase industrial AC motors should be checked against the current EMA listing, rating range, and minimum class before import.
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly uses GB 18613 for motor efficiency grades with IE class naming aligned to IEC 60034-30-1, plus factory test records and nameplate efficiency information.
rows.gap: IE class naming is not enough. Singapore compliance needs the EMA-covered product determination, accepted test evidence, registration where applicable, and rating-specific confirmation that the motor meets Singapore MEPS.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for covered motor products listed under EMA MEPS
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for motors within GB 18613 scope

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Confirm EMA MEPS scope and minimum IE class for the exact motor before shipment; a China GB 18613 IE marking is not by itself a Singapore MEPS registration.

rows.target_requirement: Singapore evidence should support the declared motor efficiency using SS or IEC 60034 test methods acceptable to the Singapore responsible supplier and regulator. Test reports should tie the tested model to the imported model, rated voltage and frequency, pole count, output, and duty.
rows.china_equivalent: China files may include GB 18613 declarations and GB or GB/T efficiency test reports for the motor family, with cooling baseline evidence under GB 12665 where relevant.
rows.gap: A China-only efficiency report may need a crosswalk to IEC 60034 test conditions and Singapore-rated supply. Any mismatch in voltage, frequency, model family, or tested configuration can undermine EMA registration or market-surveillance evidence.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory evidence for covered MEPS registration and post-market verification
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory evidence for GB 18613 conformity where within China scope

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Build a Singapore test-evidence pack around the exact imported model and SS or IEC method; do not rely on unmatched China family reports without technical justification.

rows.target_requirement: For equipment listed under Singapore energy-efficiency controls, the responsible supplier must complete the required EMA registration and energy-label process before supply. Label or database information should match the model, rating, declared efficiency, and supplier record.
rows.china_equivalent: China export files may include efficiency grade marking, GB test reports, CCC details where applicable, and Chinese nameplate or packaging information, but these are not Singapore energy-label records.
rows.gap: If the motor or motor-driven equipment is listed for Singapore energy labelling, the China energy grade cannot substitute for local registration, label format, supplier declaration, or database listing.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for listed equipment requiring Singapore energy label registration
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory only where China efficiency marking or CCC marking rules apply

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Check whether the final product is on Singapore energy-label lists; if yes, complete the EMA registration and labelling route before local supply.

rows.requirement: EMC for Motor Drives and Assemblies
rows.target_requirement: Standalone industrial motors normally present limited EMC risk, but VFDs, starters, controllers, power electronics, and assembled motor systems may need EMC evidence suitable for Singapore installation and IMDA or other regulator expectations. Industrial installation conditions, cable lengths, filters, and enclosure configuration should be documented.
rows.china_equivalent: China export files may include GB EMC reports for VFDs or control electronics, CCC documentation for in-scope low-voltage equipment, and motor GB efficiency files, but these are not Singapore IMDA acceptance records.
china_standards: GB EMC standards for drives or electronics
rows.gap: Singapore review should focus on the assembled system and any drive electronics, not just the motor frame. China EMC or CCC reports need model, configuration, and installation matching before they can support Singapore market files.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where the imported product includes regulated electronics, radio, telecom, or EMC-relevant assemblies
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory where China EMC or CCC scope applies

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] For motor-plus-drive products, prepare Singapore-facing EMC evidence for the actual assembly and installation conditions; a bare-motor file is usually incomplete.

rows.target_requirement: If a motor controller, VFD, gateway, sensor, or condition-monitoring module includes Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, cellular, or other radio functions, Singapore IMDA equipment registration or conformity requirements may apply before import or sale.
target_standards: IMDA telecommunication and radio-communication equipment requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China files may include SRRC, NAL, CCC, or GB reports for wireless modules and control products, in addition to GB motor efficiency evidence.
china_standards: SRRC for radio modules where applicable
rows.gap: China radio approvals do not replace IMDA equipment registration. The Singapore file should identify the exact radio module, frequency bands, power levels, firmware constraints, and host integration.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where IMDA-regulated radio or telecom functions are present
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory where China SRRC, NAL, CCC, or other radio scope applies

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Any wireless monitoring or control feature should trigger an IMDA scope check; do not treat motor efficiency approval as covering radio compliance.

rows.target_requirement: Singapore importers should confirm HS classification, responsible supplier status, EMA MEPS registration where applicable, IMDA approval where electronics or radio functions are included, and any sector-specific installation controls before placing industrial motors on the market.
rows.china_equivalent: China exporters usually provide commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin where needed, GB efficiency report, CCC certificate where applicable, and nameplate or datasheet information.
rows.gap: Singapore market access is not a document handover of China certificates. The importer must complete Singapore-specific registrations and retain regulator-facing evidence tied to the supplied model.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for import and supply where Singapore registration, customs, energy, or IMDA requirements apply
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for China export and domestic conformity files where applicable

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Assign a Singapore importer or responsible supplier and complete Singapore-specific registration checks before commercial supply.

rows.target_requirement: Singapore uses a 400/230 V, three-phase, 50 Hz supply environment. The 50 Hz frequency matches common China motors, but Singapore three-phase nominal voltage is 400 V rather than China's common 380 V industrial rating, so thermal rise, torque, efficiency, and insulation margins should be checked.
rows.china_equivalent: China industrial motors are commonly rated for 380 V three-phase, 50 Hz, with GB 18613 efficiency declarations and GB or CCC nameplate data tied to the China-rated supply.
rows.gap: The frequency match reduces one conversion issue, but the voltage difference can still affect losses, heating, starting current, torque, and nameplate claims. Singapore files should show 400 V suitability or dual-rating evidence.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory practical design and safety requirement for installation on Singapore supply
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory practical rating requirement for China 380 V 50 Hz supply where sold domestically

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Treat 400 V 50 Hz suitability as a technical check even when the motor already has China 380 V 50 Hz GB evidence.

rows.target_requirement: Singapore is known for strict market surveillance and regulator follow-up. CCC is not recognized as Singapore approval, so importers should keep Singapore-specific registration records, technical files, labels, test reports, and supplier declarations available for inspection.
rows.china_equivalent: CCC certificates and China GB reports support China domestic conformity and may help explain factory quality controls, but they do not create Singapore authorization.
rows.gap: The core gap is recognition. China marks and certificates may be supporting evidence, but Singapore regulators will expect Singapore-relevant scope decisions, accepted test evidence, and local supplier accountability.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory expectation for regulated supply and post-market inspection readiness
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory in China only where CCC or GB regulatory scope applies

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Do not market CCC as Singapore approval; maintain a separate Singapore evidence file for EMA, IMDA, customs, and market-surveillance response.

rows.target_requirement: Singapore safety files for industrial motors should demonstrate suitability for the intended installation using SS or IEC 60034 evidence, including insulation system, temperature rise, enclosure protection, cooling method, terminals, earthing, and nameplate warnings. Building-integrated equipment may also need BCA or project-level compliance review.
target_standards: BCA building requirements where integrated into building works
rows.china_equivalent: China files commonly include GB 12665 cooling and performance evidence, GB 18613 efficiency evidence, type-test data, and CCC documents where low-voltage motor scope applies.
rows.gap: China safety and performance evidence should be mapped to SS or IEC clauses and Singapore installation conditions. Where the motor is part of building services, BCA or project specifications can add requirements beyond the motor certificate.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for safe installation, supplier due diligence, and project acceptance; BCA applies where building integration triggers project controls
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory where China GB or CCC safety and performance scope applies

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Prepare a Singapore safety file mapped to SS or IEC 60034 and the actual installation; CCC or China GB files alone are not a Singapore safety clearance.

rows.target_requirement: Singapore-facing documentation should include clear English nameplate and instructions covering rating, voltage, frequency, phase, efficiency, insulation class, IP rating, duty, wiring, protection, maintenance, and safe use with VFDs where applicable. Data should match EMA, IMDA, and supplier records.
rows.china_equivalent: China nameplates and manuals may be based on GB 18613, GB 12665, CCC marking, and domestic wiring or warning conventions, sometimes with Chinese-only documentation.
rows.gap: Singapore supply needs English, Singapore-rated, model-specific documentation. China-only labels, 380 V-only plates, or mismatched VFD instructions can create installation, registration, and surveillance problems.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory practical requirement for safe supply, registration consistency, and market-surveillance readiness
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory where China GB, CCC, or domestic marking rules apply

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Update labels and instructions for Singapore supply, especially 400 V 50 Hz use and any VFD or wireless configuration.
